title: What can you say about coenzyme Q10 in your ads and on your site?
summary: The library supports 2 wordings for coenzyme Q10; the strongest is "Helps maintain cardiovascular health" (moderate, 30-300 mg a day). Avoid wording that names or implies a disease, a drug or a treatment, such as "Treats heart failure or heart disease".

supported_wordings.why: Health Canada lists it at 30-300 mg a day (15-300 mg for ubiquinol); no other listed source covers it.
supported_wordings.dose_details: Adults 18 and older. Health Canada: 30-300 mg a day of coenzyme Q10. Its ubiquinol monograph gives 15-300 mg a day of ubiquinol for the same use, so a ubiquinol product at 15-30 mg a day shows here as below the range.

supported_wordings.wording: Provides an antioxidant that helps protect cells against damage from free radicals.
supported_wordings.why: Health Canada sets a maximum dose only; no other listed source covers it.
supported_wordings.dose_details: Adults 18 and older; Health Canada sets a maximum of 300 mg a day for coenzyme Q10 and for ubiquinol.

wordings_to_avoid.wording: Treats heart failure or heart disease
wordings_to_avoid.why: Names diseases; the supported wording is maintaining cardiovascular health.
Names a disease marker. FDA's 2000 rule (page 1006) counts a claim that a product promotes low blood pressure as a disease claim.
Names a disease. Health Canada's migraine use is a Canada only note.
Implies treating a side effect of a drug, a medical condition; no listed source supports it.

evidence_strengths.strong: At least two listed sources support it independently at a comparable dose and form, and none disagrees.
evidence_strengths.moderate: One listed source supports it as an evidence-based use at that dose, and no listed source disagrees.
evidence_strengths.limited: The only support is traditional use, the sources disagree, or the source itself calls the evidence weak.

reasons_to_avoid.drug: names a drug or presents the product as one
reasons_to_avoid.treatment: promises to treat, cure or prevent a condition

disclaimer: Not legal advice. This guide shows the wording that published evidence supports at a daily dose, from the sources linked below; it is not a ruling on any claim. Your own product, its form and dose, and your own evidence still need to match the wording you use.
